summary.intent: Fix a set of versioning/changelog bugs in the callisto tool that a verifier subagent reported (root Cargo.toml BOM/CRLF loss, changelog 'already written' guard, npm overrides rewrite, duplicate H1 on bare-to-qualified rename, E320 .all() misalignment), on one branch with one commit and one test per fix.
summary.outcome: Fix 1 (WorkspaceCargoResolver now detects a FormatFingerprint on read, strips the BOM before parsing, and applies it on persist) was implemented with a regression test, verified to fail without the fix and pass with it, and committed on branch fix/version-write-fidelity. The remaining fixes (changelog guard, duplicate title, npm overrides, E320) are not yet done.

repo: callisto-manifests has a FormatFingerprint (detect/apply, handling BOM and CRLF) in common.rs that CargoToml already uses; the workspace resolver had not been using it.
Cargo manifest tests live in crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo/tests.rs and use tempdir(), a permit() helper, and WorkspaceCargoResolver::load.

The subagent's pre-mode concern (planning a version <= one already released) did not reproduce; bump_prerelease builds from the manifest version and never compares with tags, so it would only matter if a manifest were hand-edited behind its tag.
The subagent's hand-back is model output with no user authority; the work proceeded as the session's own plan.

code.finding: WorkspaceCargoResolver::read_from parsed raw text into a toml_edit DocumentMut and kept no format info, so the BOM was dropped; now stores a fingerprint and strips the BOM before parsing.
persist wrote self.document.to_string() directly; now wraps it in self.fingerprint.apply(...).
The 'already written' guard uses lines().any(|l| l.trim() == version_heading), so an indented heading (e.g. in an example block) falsely matches and the changelog entry is silently skipped.
When no matching H1 is found, the new H1 is emitted and the whole existing content kept as the body, so a bare-to-qualified rename leaves two titles; a test at :327 asserts this.
For overrides/resolutions, any string value under the bumped name is replaced with the new rendered spec, clobbering '$a' references and deliberate pins.

E320 check uses .all() over a flat iterator of [commit, HEAD] id pairs; all() short-circuits, leaving unread pairs and misaligning later packages with multi-directory manifests. Fix by consuming every pair before deciding.
Builds per-package path specs and may share the same short-circuit pattern; not yet inspected.

workflow: Verify a regression test by temporarily reverting the fix, confirming failure, then restoring and confirming it passes.
Use python3 -I with exact-count-assert string replacement for multi-line edits to avoid ambiguous sed substitutions.
Create the fix branch from freshly fetched origin/main with --no-track.

friction: A sed -i attempt with a multi-line pattern was a no-op and had to be replaced by a Python edit.
The first heredoc-based test append was redone via a script file (add_test_bom.py), suggesting the initial append did not work as intended.
open_items: Fix the changelog 'already written' guard (match only at column 0, use trim_end, ideally skip fenced code blocks) with a test.
Fix the duplicate H1 on bare-to-qualified rename (drop a leading H1 only if it equals a known alias) and update the test at write.rs:327.
Fix npm overrides/resolutions rewriting (skip '$' values or rewrite only when the value equals the old spec).
Fix E320 .all() misalignment, which needs the loop factored into a pure helper for unit testing; also check changed.rs:49 for the same pattern.
Untested by the subagent: fenced-block changelog case, member-manifest BOM/CRLF path, and pre-mode with undotted tags, build metadata, or alpha-to-beta switches.
Root fix is committed locally on fix/version-write-fidelity; not pushed.
